description: Insecure Route Table Configuration in Outposts Local Gateway Misconfigured route tables in the Local Gateway could allow unauthorized traffic flows between different network segments or to/from external networks. This could bypass intended network isolation and security controls. An attacker who gains access to one subnet could leverage overly permissive routes to move laterally to other subnets or access the EKS control plane, potentially compromising the entire cluster.
references: recommendation: Implement least-privilege route table configurations

description: Insufficient Worker Node Isolation Without proper network policies and security group configurations, worker nodes can freely communicate with each other, potentially allowing compromised nodes to affect others. If an attacker compromises a pod or node, they could use the lack of isolation to spread laterally across the cluster, potentially accessing sensitive workloads on other nodes.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1210 - Exploitation of Remote Services
recommendation: Implement strict node isolation using security groups and network policies

description: Inadequate Pod Identity Management Without proper Pod Identity configuration, pods might run with excessive permissions or be able to assume roles they shouldn't have access to. An attacker who compromises a pod could leverage overly permissive IAM roles to access AWS services or resources beyond what the pod should be able to access.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1548 - Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
recommendation: Implement proper Pod Identity configuration with least privilege
